subject: Re: 🔵{Brand} & MobUpps
body:
Hi RECIPIENT_NAME,
Circling back on my earlier note about recovering drop-off shoppers for {Brand}. Amazon Prime went live in South Africa on 3 June and runs its first local Prime Day from 23 to 29 June, so your browsers will price-check on Amazon.co.za this week before they check out. That is when win-back quality decides your cost, with ecommerce CAC running between 68 and 84 dollars per first customer. We hold a control group out, so recovered purchases show as incremental to buyers who would have returned anyway. Worth comparing against your current mix?
angle: fresh angle: Amazon Prime SA launch + Prime Day 23-29 June (sourced) + ecommerce CAC 68-84 USD band
register_notes: Stage 2 EN ecommerce retargeting South Africa, native English. References prior in first sentence and acknowledges second follow-up. Fresh angle = timely sourced development (Amazon Prime SA launch 3 June 2026 + first SA Prime Day 23-29 June 2026, bizcommunity) naming peer Amazon.co.za from brand_candidates, plus real ecommerce CAC band 68-84 USD (ringly 2026). MobUpps holdout incrementality referenced with no figure. Exactly one question mark; no sign-off; no em-dash; no curly quotes; no hedge before a number; no 'X, not Y'. Market-context numbers are real and web-verified with URLs in enrichment_sources.
